result.title: Instance-dependent sequential limits as an exact information ledger
result.summary: Instance-dependent limits for bandit regret, sequential tests, best-arm identification and Markov decision processes are proved by one chain. It runs from a divergence decomposition through data processing to a statistic, a testing step that turns a class guarantee into a requirement on the history, and optimization over alternatives and allocations. Only the first step is an identity. This work writes the chain as an exact ledger. By the chain rule, data processing loses exactly a conditional divergence, which vanishes for arms in natural exponential families at the per-arm counts and reward sums. A one-parameter family of martingale identities extends the decomposition to every tilt between two instances. The classical limits follow by relaxations with named defects. All defects but the asymptotic step's can be computed from an algorithm's own runs, the uniform quantification's only when the class guarantee is a number. On seven published sources, from movie ratings to engine replacement, the ledger locates the difference between standard algorithms and the classical limits. For identification among trained models and for Wald's test the largest term is usually the uniform quantification's.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 bandit regret、序贯检验、最佳臂识别与 MDP 的 instance-dependent 极限统一写成一条从散度分解、数据处理到检验与优化的“精确信息账本”，并给出一族鞅恒等式及可计算的缺陷项，用于在多个应用数据源上定位算法与经典极限的差距。
AI.relevance_reason: 其序贯证据累积与 Wald 检验式停止、信息账本和缺陷分解，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的停止决策与信息—计算成本核算提供概念工具，但需核查如何映射到 latent 状态与视觉证据筛选。
